meta.title: Zambia Government Operating Model
meta.baseline: Government Scope Reference Model - International Baseline (14 domains, 91 SAs, 501 concepts)
meta.note: Built from the international baseline + Zambia mapping, per the answered decision register (artifact 48KKXwXqNYgkmwNDGdXg7i). The 8 grade-A entities had their source links and Act names independently opened and confirmed on 28 Oct 2026 (7 Acts verified; the pensions entry corrected to the Public Service Pensions Fund). The 5 grade-C and 3 external entities are NOT primary-verified, and whole-of-government reconciliation (Yellow Book, PACRA, cabinet gazette, Constitution, local-authority and traditional registers) remains in the validation backlog. Every entity carries its evidence grade. v1.1.0 adds the two source figures and the Zambia-structure-to-generic mapping. v1.3.0 adds the Master & Reference Data / ownership-stewardship overlay: the governance metamodel, 8 accountability roles, 9 foundational + 14 sector master-data domains, an 18-row ownership-allocation matrix, reference-data classes, the governance-artifact chain, RACI decision rights, the national registers, the data-contract spec, and the gaps/roadmap.

entity_types.definition: Highest-order constitutional division of state authority
Public office created directly by the Constitution
Collegial institution established constitutionally with defined public powers
Cabinet portfolio and central executive organization for a sphere of policy
Administrative unit performing a defined mandate within a ministry or public institution
Body corporate established by an Act for a defined mandate

resolution_rules: Official statistics stewardship sits in Domain 1 (not Education/Research or Domain 14); technology platforms for statistics stay in Domain 14.
A regulator is placed in its regulated-sector domain; licensing, inspection and enforcement are mapped as capabilities, not Subject Areas.
A public enterprise uses its operating sector as primary placement; state ownership and fiscal-risk relationships are recorded separately against Domain 5.
Smart Zambia Institute is placed in Domain 14, even though its services support every domain.
The data-protection body is placed in Domain 1 (public oversight); privacy controls and incidents cross-reference Domain 14.
Traditional governance is not subsumed under local government without explicit constitutional or statutory evidence.
A ministry can change name or portfolio while its Domains and Subject Areas remain stable (entity vs mandate).

metamodel_constructs.definition: Durable jurisdiction-neutral sphere of governmental responsibility; not an organization.
Cohesive, domain-specific information grouping with a semantic boundary and stewardship home.
Stable noun or phenomenon about which government records facts.
Governance classification grouping reusable master entities around a stable subject (e.g. Person or Land). References concepts from several Subject Areas but does not replace them.
Identifiable, reusable entity with lifecycle, identifiers, attributes, relationships and cross-process reuse.
Context in which an entity participates (Taxpayer, Employer, Patient, Supplier). A role should not automatically become a separate master domain.
Controlled codes, classifications, permissible values, hierarchies or mappings used to classify, constrain or interpret data.
Legally or administratively recognized source for a defined entity, attribute, status or code set.
Operational system designated to preserve authoritative records for a specified scope. One system need not be authoritative for every attribute.
Trusted, possibly composite representation from identity resolution, source precedence and provenance; not automatically the legal record.
Institution or executive accountable for meaning, lawful purpose, quality expectations, release and authoritative-source decisions.
Function legally empowered to establish the entity, identity, status, registration, license or controlled value.
Maintains definitions, values, rules, data quality, exceptions, mappings and lifecycle changes.
Accountable for the business operation of the designated System of Record.
Operates storage, access, security, backup, integration, monitoring and recovery.
Technically publishes the authoritative data product or approved extract; may differ from the Data Owner.
Governed, consumable representation with owner, semantics, quality rules, service expectations, access controls and lifecycle.

roles.definition: Senior executive accountable for the data domain and its appropriate use.
Establishes and authorises official master or reference lists (e.g. national registers, code lists).
Ensures business quality, fit for purpose and ongoing maintenance.
Operates the authoritative source system(s) for the data.
Provides secure access (e.g. APIs, data products) and technical operations.
Accountable for appropriate use of data in their domain or service.
Sets direction, policy, standards and oversight for government data.
Ensures legal, privacy, security and classification requirements are met.

gaps: Public Body Register ownership is unresolved.
PACRA, land, address, vehicle, health, education, court and local/traditional-register allocations require primary legal validation.
Risk of duplicate catalogues, registries, exchanges and open-data inventories.
Ministry reorganizations can orphan ownership if assignments use ministry names rather than legal functions.
Analytical copies may be mistaken for authoritative masters.
Cross-domain roles may create competing identifiers.
Personal identity, household, health and beneficiary integration creates material privacy and matching risk.
External standards may be locally copied without version, adoption or crosswalk governance.
roadmap: Establish the national registers: Authoritative Source, Master Data, Reference Data, Data Contract, API Product.
Approve the metamodel and decision-rights standard.
Certify first-wave masters: civil identity, legal entity, public body, administrative geography/address, taxpayer, land parcel, government service.
Validate legal mandates and SoRs through Acts, Gazettes, official registers and named system-owner attestations.
Register ownership and artifact profiles for ZRA, Department of National Registration, NAPSA, PSPF, NHIMA, ZamStats, Bank of Zambia and ZICTA.
Pilot governed sharing using two or three high-reuse, legally clear masters (not a universal central database).
Publish minimum Data Contract and API standards, with catalogue registration and automated conformance evidence.
Introduce sector waves: health providers/medicines; vehicles/operators; education providers/qualifications; social protection; regulated entities.
Reconcile duplicates and identifiers, preserving authoritative source IDs and cross-reference mappings rather than destructive replacement.
Operate assurance continuously: ownership coverage, source certification, API adoption, contract conformance, deprecated-code use, quality breaches, unresolved exceptions.
